server: throwaway instance on a spare port, hostssl only, certificate for DNS name localhost signed by a drill CA; the mismatched-host case connects to 127.0.0.1, which the certificate does not name

refusal_reasons.plaintext_connection: error: error returned from database: pg_hba.conf rejects connection for host 127.0.0.1, user trestle, database postgres, no encryption
refusal_reasons.verify_full_with_untrusted_ca: error: error communicating with database: invalid peer certificate: UnknownIssuer
refusal_reasons.verify_full_with_mismatched_host: error: error communicating with database: invalid peer certificate: certificate not valid for name 127.0.0.1; certificate is only valid for DnsName(localhost)
refusal_reasons.production_boot_with_require: - DATABASE_URL must use sslmode=verify-full for a non-local database in production (require and verify-ca do not check the server's identity; set sslrootcert for a private CA)
refusal_reasons.production_boot_with_verify_ca: - DATABASE_URL must use sslmode=verify-full for a non-local database in production (require and verify-ca do not check the server's identity; set sslrootcert for a private CA)

weaker_modes_observed.verify_ca_with_mismatched_host_detail: error: error communicating with database: invalid peer certificate: certificate not valid for name 127.0.0.1; certificate is only valid for DnsName(localhost)

notes: weaker_modes_observed is informational, not asserted: require connecting to a server signed by an untrusted CA is the SR-03 weakness. With this driver build verify-ca also refuses a mismatched IP address (the hostname-skipping verifier does not recognize the newer rustls error), but that is incidental and version-dependent, so production accepts only verify-full for a non-local database. The boot cases use the unresolvable host db.invalid: verify-full passes the boot checks and then fails to connect; require and verify-ca are refused before any connection.
